title: Pashpasha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In the [Jerusalem Talmud, Shevi'it ch. 6, halakha 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sheviit.6.1.14): Hyman quotes, “Pashpasha. Rabbi Yose said: I asked Rabbi Abba.” And [the commentary] [Penei Moshe](https://www.sefaria.org/Penei_Moshe_on_Jerusalem_Talmud_Sheviit.6.1.14.3) explains that it is the name of a sage, but Hyman considers a place-name more likely.

Ahavat Tziyon explains pashpasha instead as an expression of the need for examination, comparing [Ketubot 110b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.110b.2): “[A pleasant dwelling puts a person to the test](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.110b.2).”

notes.text: Penei Moshe takes Pashpasha as a sage. Hyman prefers a place-name. Ahavat Tziyon gives a verbal explanation. The [Gemara’s explanation](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.110b.5) understands the test as illness caused by a change of habit.

In the linked Jerusalem Talmud, Pashpasha speaks before Rabbi Yose and says that he asked Rabbi Acha, who permitted it. Penei Moshe calls Pashpasha the name of a man and also gives Rabbi Acha. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3014&lang=en) gives the same speakers and Rabbi Acha. Hyman’s quotation has Rabbi Yose speaking and names Rabbi Abba.
